_comment: Garment families. A family groups SHAPES of the same garment so the combinator can be asked for one and never return a different garment that shares the slot. Generic: a new family is a new entry here plus bases that name it, with no engine change.

beret.classification_reason: The only ingested shape, beret_01, comes from hyoung_hats_24, whose provenance and licence are unestablished. Architecture, conversion and testing only; not shippable until the source is identified.

pools._comment: Gated on motif_class, not on decal name. A flower authored next month is legal wherever `flower` already is, with nobody editing this file. RarePlus keeps `pin` from Rare because the formal/smart styles have no flower, bow or feather in the pool at all; without it a formal RarePlus beret would carry LESS decoration than a formal Rare one, which the batch caught.

refused._comment: Recorded with reasons, the way authored/source_bases/cap2/overlay_marks.json records why a mark was dropped. A refusal nobody wrote down gets re-proposed six weeks later.
refused.letters: unreadable below ~6px per glyph; a beret crown gives 3
refused.text: same, and it dates the asset
refused.logos: detail density cannot survive the 20x20 frame
refused.crests: same, and it implies a fiction the pack does not have
refused.faces: reads as noise at gameplay scale
refused.animal_faces: only legible if it fills the crown, which stops it being a motif
refused._overturned: `pom` and `tassel` were refused in Milestone 1 on the grounds that a pom reads as a knit cap. The user's reference batch shows a white pom on a beret, so the reference wins: pom is allowed at RarePlus. Tassel stays refused -- nothing in the reference shows one.

optional_pending_review._comment: On the approved list but not enabled: each needs art that survives the integration pass before it may be rolled.
optional_pending_review.moon_pin: no art in the pool at all
optional_pending_review.gem_brooch: gem_oval is crown_face-only; needs a side variant
optional_pending_review.patch: patch_square is 12 cells, which eats a whole Rare budget

known_gaps._comment: Found by tools/build_beret_batch.py in Milestone 2. Recorded rather than papered over: the fix is a new decal, which is library expansion, not architecture.

beret_02_RarePlus_surface.effect: RarePlus carries one piece where Rare carries two, so richness dips at the top tier for this shape.
beret_02_RarePlus_surface.cause: The RarePlus surface classes are woven_trim, band and badge. Both band pieces are 6 wide and beret_02's side band zone is 5, so they fail the all-views rule; brooch_round is a surface motif zoned to `side`, which overhangs the crown edge, so it fails containment.
beret_02_RarePlus_surface.fix_belongs_to: library expansion — a premium surface trim shaped for beret_02's shallow crown and narrow side band
beret_02_RarePlus_surface.do_not: widen the RarePlus pool with a Rare-grade class to make the number go up; that flattens the ladder instead of filling the gap

cute_beret.label: cute beret
cute_beret.intent: Reproduce the design language of the user's reference batch: soft puffy domes, muted pastel bodies with a darker band of their own colour, visible material differences, and one small warm accent.
cute_beret.weighting_note: Weights bias the roll toward the reference; they never restrict. Anything legal for the tier can still appear, which is what keeps a batch from collapsing into twelve copies of the reference.
cute_beret.class_deny_reason: beret_03 carries its band and rim in its own art, exactly as the reference does -- there the band is a darker shade of the hat's own colour, not a separate piece. An overlay band on top of that draws a second, brighter bar across the crown and is the one thing that made an early batch stop looking like the reference. Denied for this profile only; the classes stay available to every other profile and family.
cute_beret.shape_note: The reference shows ONE silhouette across all twelve cells: its variation is material, palette and decoration, not shape. So the profile is dominated by beret_03, with beret_02 at low weight for occasional relief. beret_01 is not in this profile at all -- it is a flatter, harder-edged beret that belongs to a different look. Neither is restricted: both remain fully available to any other profile.
